Long-term trend temporal base value

Source: R/temporal_base.R
temporal_base_trend.Rd

Estimates a non-periodic, long-term background multiplier over the whole study horizon. With resp_weight = NULL (default) this returns a flat trend (basevalue = 1 everywhere) - the Loop-0 initial guess in the original script, where the weighted-smoothing loop was disabled and the trend was left flat until the first E-step. With resp_weight supplied (one EM responsibility weight per event, e.g. trend.fun(days) * mub.events / lambda.at.events), it reproduces the Loop-k weighted Gaussian smoother with boundary (edge-effect) correction via stats::pnorm().

Usage

temporal_base_trend(
  events,
  resp_weight = NULL,
  bandwidth = 150,
  chunk_size = 500
)

Arguments

events

A "semihawkes_events" object from prepare_events().

resp_weight

Optional numeric vector, one entry per event in events$events, e.g. an EM E-step responsibility weight. If NULL (default), only the day-count correction weight is used (the Loop-0 initial-guess behaviour).

bandwidth

Gaussian smoothing bandwidth (in days); default 150, matching the original script.

chunk_size

Number of distinct event days processed per chunk when resp_weight is supplied, to bound peak memory use for long study periods; default 500.

Value

A list of class "semihawkes_temporal_base" with elements breaks (events$time.marks), basevalue (normalized to mean 1), period (NA, i.e. non-periodic), and fun (a vectorized function of days, 0 outside [0, TT]).

Details

Events fall on whole days, so the weights of events on the same day are added up first, and the smoothed curve is evaluated on a grid of one day, or bandwidth / 100 days if that is finer, then interpolated linearly to events$time.marks. That changes the curve by at most about (step / bandwidth)^2 / 8 of its value: 6 parts in a million for the default bandwidth. When the grid would be as fine as the time marks, the curve is evaluated at the time marks directly.

References

Zhuang & Mateu (2019); see spHawkes-package.

Examples

ev <- prepare_events(sim_events, sim_region, date_col = "date",
                     end_date = "2022-01-01")
#> The modelled study period ends on 2021-12-29, the day after the last event. `end_date` (2022-01-01) is used only to select events and to label outputs.
# Without weights: the flat initial guess used before the first EM step
flat <- temporal_base_trend(ev)
range(flat$basevalue)
#> [1] 1 1
# With weights (here every event weighted equally): a smoothed trend
trend <- temporal_base_trend(ev, resp_weight = rep(1, nrow(ev$events)))
plot(trend$breaks, trend$basevalue, type = "l",
     xlab = "Days since start", ylab = "Trend multiplier")
